summary.name: Reframed
summary.one_liner: Reframed is an open-source macOS screen recorder with a built-in timeline editor for trimming, zooming, styling, captioning, and exporting recordings.
use_cases: recording software demos and app walkthroughs
creating tutorial videos with zoom and cursor effects
recording iPhone or iPad demos over USB
exporting ProRes or GIF clips from screen captures
recording talking-head webcam segments alongside screen
summary.what_it_does: Reframed records a full screen, a single window, a custom region, or a connected iOS device, with optional system audio, microphone, and a resizable webcam overlay at up to 60 fps. Cursor position and clicks are sampled at 120 Hz separately from video, which feeds the cursor overlay and zoom automation in the editor. The built-in timeline editor lets you trim video and audio tracks separately, add manual or auto-detected zoom keyframes, apply backgrounds and padding, mark fullscreen webcam segments, and reduce microphone noise. Captions are generated on-device with WhisperKit and can be burned in or exported as SRT/VTT. Export supports MP4, MOV, GIF, H.264, H.265, ProRes 422 and 4444, with scaling to 4K, 1080p, or 720p and multi-core rendering.
notable: Built-in timeline editor with auto and manual zoom, cursor-follow, and spotlight effects
Cursor metadata sampled at 120 Hz to drive zoom and cursor overlay
On-device captions via WhisperKit with SRT/VTT export
Records connected iPhones and iPads over USB
caveats: macOS only per the page; iOS recording requires a USB-connected device
Auto-zoom and captions depend on the editor's features and chosen model size
